name: Canals (Stormwind City)
summary: Walkers and anglers share the paths beside Stormwind's Canals, winding between the city's districts.

sections.title: Arteries of the Capital
sections.body: You can follow the Canals from the Trade District's markets to Old Town's aged alleys, the cathedral gardens, and the Dwarven District. Stone bridges and archways cross the water, while paths pass the Gallina Winery, tailor shops, and quiet homes. Merchants and fishermen use these waterways. Beneath the streets, the fortified Stockade entrance holds Stormwind's most dangerous criminals and rebels.

sections.title: A Gruesome History and Lurking Shadows
sections.body: The Horde sacked Stormwind during the First War, leaving the Canals in ruins. The waterways were restored as the capital rose again after the Second War. Now they are clean and repaired, though rumors speak of a massive albino crocolisk beneath the docks.

faq.q: What happened to the canals during the First War?
faq.answer: The Horde sacked Stormwind during the First War, leaving the city and its waterways in ruins. The Canals were restored when the capital was rebuilt after the Second War.

faq.q: Is there really a monster in the Stormwind canals?
faq.answer: No one can say for certain. Rumors tell of a massive white crocolisk lurking in the waterways, though guards and residents often dismiss the tales as tavern gossip. Reports continue, and adventurers are warned not to fall in.

faq.q: Where is the entrance to the Stockade located?
faq.answer: The Stockade entrance lies along the canal's northernmost stretch around the Mage Quarter, guarded by the Stormwind City Guard.

faq.q: Can players swim through the canals to travel around Stormwind?
faq.answer: You can swim through the Canals, then climb back to the street by stone stairs or docks along the waterside paths.

angles.text: As an aspiring cook, you can fish along the quiet canal banks within the safety of the capital's walls.
As an Alliance member, you can see how Stormwind's Canals were restored after the First War's ruins, as the capital became a working, picturesque city.
